newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed on Monday in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.

"Government securities ended narrowly mixed amid uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 3.37/3.32 percent compared with last Friday's yield of 3.50/3.45 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.86/2.81 percent against 3.02/2.97 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.15/98.20 from last Friday's close of S$98.03/98.08, May 2002 at S$99.25/99.30 versus S$99.00/99.05 and June 2003 at S$94.28/94.33 against S$94.00/94.05.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 4-1/4 4 percent from last Friday's 4-1/8 4 percent.
